_comment: Sergas Group, from the 2026 brand refresh. Only the values the brand book actually fixes are pinned here; everything else is left to derivation, which also darkens any colour used as text on light stock until it clears WCAG AA. That last part matters for this brand specifically: the brand book records that white-on-orange and blue-on-navy both fail contrast, so pinning those pairings by hand would ship a book nobody can read.

colors._comment: Navy is the surface and orange is the action colour — that split is the brand book's, not a design choice made here. Medium Blue does large-shape and decorative work, so it lands on `secondary` rather than competing with orange for emphasis.
colors._curtain_comment: Only the base cloth is pinned. Pinning its lit crest and its trough as well set the trough to the same navy as the stage void, which made the cloth-against-void contrast and the fold-against-fold contrast the identical sum — 3.11 both ways — and the curtain read as stripes on a dark field rather than as lit fabric. Derivation gets the tonal spread right; the brand only fixes the colour.
colors._paper_comment: Warm-neutral stock rather than pure white. A navy book printed on #FFFFFF reads as a screenshot of a website; paper that is very slightly off-white is what makes the spread read as a physical page under the stage light.

fonts._comment: Owners Text is the brand's one Latin family — Medium carries headings, Regular carries body, and weight is the whole hierarchy. `display_files` names the subsetted woff2 the build embeds; without it the stack would resolve to a system fallback on every machine that has never had the licensed font installed, which is every machine that receives the book.
